content:
# Disagreement Log — 2 Maccabees Chapter 3

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Total Disagreements:** 22

---

## Disagreement 001 — v. 1: City's condition

- **EMET:** "inhabited with all peace"
- **LOGOS:** "at complete peace"
- **PNEUMA:** "at complete peace"
- **Note:** EMET is more literal (*katoikeisthai meta pasēs eirēnēs*). LOGOS/PNEUMA agree on "complete peace." SOPHIA follows LOGOS/PNEUMA.

## Disagreement 002 — v. 2: Kings' gifts

- **EMET:** "glorified the temple with the finest presents"
- **LOGOS:** "glorified the temple with magnificent gifts"
- **PNEUMA:** "honored the temple with splendid gifts"
- **Note:** LOGOS and PNEUMA agree on "magnificent/splendid gifts." EMET's "finest presents" is slightly more literal. SOPHIA uses "magnificent gifts."

## Disagreement 003 — v. 6: Simon's claim about the money

- **EMET:** "the total amount of the funds was beyond counting"
- **LOGOS:** "sums so large that the total could not be counted"
- **PNEUMA:** "sums so vast they were beyond all counting"
- **Note:** PNEUMA adds "all" for rhetorical emphasis. All three convey the same meaning. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 004 — v. 6: Nature of the funds

- **EMET:** "they did not belong to the account of the sacrifices but it was possible for them to fall under the authority of the king"
- **LOGOS:** "these funds did not belong to the account of the sacrifices but could fall under the power of the king"
- **PNEUMA:** "none of it was earmarked for the sacrificial fund; it was, Simon claimed, ripe for the taking by the king"
- **Note:** PNEUMA adds "Simon claimed" — an editorial insertion not in the Greek — and uses "ripe for the taking," which is idiomatic. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 005 — v. 7: Heliodorus's role

- **EMET:** "who was in charge of his affairs"
- **LOGOS:** "his chief minister"
- **PNEUMA:** "his chief minister"
- **Note:** EMET's "in charge of his affairs" is more literal. LOGOS/PNEUMA agree on "chief minister." SOPHIA uses "chief minister" for clarity.

## Disagreement 006 — v. 13: Heliodorus's action

- **EMET:** "he set a date and went in to direct the inspection"
- **LOGOS:** "On the day appointed, he went in to conduct the inspection"
- **PNEUMA:** "He set a date and went in to inventory the funds"
- **Note:** PNEUMA's "inventory" is more specific than "inspection." LOGOS's "on the day appointed" is more formal. SOPHIA uses LOGOS phrasing.

## Disagreement 007 — v. 14: Priests' appeal

- **EMET:** "called toward heaven upon him who had given the law about deposits"
- **LOGOS:** "called out to heaven upon him who had given the law concerning deposits"
- **PNEUMA:** "cried out to heaven — to the God who had instituted the sacred trust of deposits"
- **Note:** PNEUMA specifies "God" and paraphrases "sacred trust." EMET/LOGOS use "him who" — preserving the indirect reference. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 008 — v. 15: High priest's appearance

- **EMET:** "to see the appearance of the high priest was to be wounded at heart"
- **LOGOS:** "to see the appearance of the high priest was itself to be wounded at heart"
- **PNEUMA:** "Watching the high priest was painful in itself"
- **Note:** PNEUMA compresses; LOGOS adds "itself" for emphasis. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 009 — v. 16: "inward agony"

- **EMET:** "the pain lodged in his heart"
- **LOGOS:** "the depth of pain lodged in his heart"
- **PNEUMA:** "the depth of the wound in his heart"
- **Note:** PNEUMA substitutes "wound" for "pain." LOGOS adds "depth." Greek *tēn kata psychēn agōnian* — the anguish of soul. SOPHIA uses "the depth of pain lodged in his heart."

## Disagreement 010 — v. 17: People's response

- **EMET:** "People hurried out of their houses in crowds"
- **LOGOS:** "People rushed out from their houses in crowds"
- **PNEUMA:** "People poured out of their houses in crowds"
- **Note:** Three different verbs for the same Greek *exerchonto*. "Rushed" (LOGOS) conveys urgency; "poured" (PNEUMA) conveys mass. SOPHIA uses "rushed out."

## Disagreement 011 — v. 18: Women in the streets

- **EMET:** "Women, girded with sackcloth below their breasts"
- **LOGOS:** "Women girded with sackcloth under their breasts"
- **PNEUMA:** "Women wrapped in sackcloth crowded the streets"
- **Note:** PNEUMA omits the "girded... under their breasts" detail, which is a specific mourning posture. EMET/LOGOS preserve this. SOPHIA retains it as theologically/culturally significant.

## Disagreement 012 — v. 18: Young women

- **EMET:** "some of the virgins who were kept indoors"
- **LOGOS:** "young women who were kept indoors"
- **PNEUMA:** "young women who had never ventured outside"
- **Note:** Greek *parthenoi* — virgins. EMET is most literal. LOGOS uses "young women" for readability. PNEUMA's "never ventured outside" is interpretive expansion. SOPHIA uses "young women."

## Disagreement 013 — v. 22: Divine title

- **EMET:** "the Sovereign of spirits and all authority"
- **LOGOS:** "the Sovereign of spirits and of all authority"
- **PNEUMA:** "the God who is Lord of spirits and Ruler of all authority"
- **Note:** PNEUMA adds "God" and "Ruler" to clarify the subject. EMET/LOGOS are closer to the Greek. SOPHIA follows EMET/LOGOS's more economical rendering.

## Disagreement 014 — v. 23: Horse's behavior

- **EMET:** "rushed furiously and struck Heliodorus with its front hooves"
- **LOGOS:** "rushed forward violently and struck Heliodorus with its front hooves"
- **PNEUMA:** "The horse reared and drove its front hooves into Heliodorus"
- **Note:** PNEUMA introduces "reared" — not in the Greek — to explain how hooves strike. EMET uses "furiously," LOGOS "violently." SOPHIA uses "rushed forward violently."

## Disagreement 015 — v. 24: Young men's description

- **EMET:** "exceedingly strong and surpassingly beautiful, with glory surrounding them"
- **LOGOS:** "exceedingly strong and surpassingly handsome, gloriously beautiful in appearance"
- **PNEUMA:** "magnificent in their strength, shining in their beauty, radiant with glory"
- **Note:** PNEUMA uses a tricolon with anaphora for poetic effect. LOGOS separates strength and beauty. SOPHIA uses "exceedingly strong and surpassingly beautiful, with glory surrounding them."

## Disagreement 016 — v. 24: "flogged"

- **EMET:** "flogged him continuously, inflicting many blows upon him"
- **LOGOS:** "flogged him continuously, each inflicting many blows"
- **PNEUMA:** "flogged him without mercy, blow after blow"
- **Note:** LOGOS clarifies "each" of the two young men. PNEUMA's "without mercy" adds interpretation. SOPHIA uses "flogged him continuously, delivering blow after blow."

## Disagreement 017 — v. 25: Heliodorus's collapse

- **EMET:** "fell suddenly to the ground and was enveloped in great darkness"
- **LOGOS:** "fell suddenly to the ground, overwhelmed by great darkness"
- **PNEUMA:** "crashed to the ground and was swallowed in deep darkness"
- **Note:** PNEUMA's "crashed" and "swallowed in deep darkness" are more vivid. EMET's "enveloped" and LOGOS's "overwhelmed" are closer to Greek *kataskotōtheis* — darkened. SOPHIA uses "overwhelmed by great darkness."

## Disagreement 018 — v. 28: Temple's reversal

- **EMET:** "was filled with joy and gladness, now that the Almighty LORD had appeared"
- **LOGOS:** "was filled with joy and gladness, because the almighty LORD had appeared"
- **PNEUMA:** "The temple filled with joy and gladness, because the almighty LORD had made himself known"
- **Note:** PNEUMA's "made himself known" (*ephanē*) is an interpretive expansion of "appeared." SOPHIA uses "had appeared."

## Disagreement 019 — v. 30: Onias's motivation

- **EMET:** "suspecting that the king might get the impression that some foul play had been perpetrated"
- **LOGOS:** "fearing that the king might suspect the Jews of foul play"
- **PNEUMA:** "Onias was worried that the king might think the Jews had done something criminal"
- **Note:** LOGOS and PNEUMA agree on the concern; EMET is more elaborate. SOPHIA uses LOGOS's economical version.

## Disagreement 020 — v. 32: "scourged from heaven"

- **EMET:** "having been scourged from heaven"
- **LOGOS:** "having been scourged from heaven"
- **PNEUMA:** "you have been struck from heaven"
- **Note:** EMET and LOGOS agree on "scourged" (*mastichtheis*). PNEUMA uses "struck," losing the specific whipping/flogging connotation. SOPHIA follows EMET/LOGOS.

## Disagreement 021 — v. 36: Heliodorus's recommendation

- **EMET:** "you will get him back well flogged, if he indeed escape with his life"
- **LOGOS:** "you will receive him back thoroughly flogged — if indeed he survives"
- **PNEUMA:** "He will come back well beaten. If he survives at all."
- **Note:** PNEUMA breaks the sentence for dramatic effect. LOGOS/EMET are more complete. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 022 — v. 37: God's relationship to the temple

- **EMET:** "who has his dwelling in heaven watches over that place himself and brings it aid"
- **LOGOS:** "who has his dwelling in heaven watches over that place himself, brings it aid"
- **PNEUMA:** "The God who dwells in heaven keeps watch over it himself. He defends it."
- **Note:** PNEUMA breaks into short sentences for rhetorical emphasis. SOPHIA retains the compound construction of LOGOS.
